obligations.title: Human oversight

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Provider obligations and quality management system
obligations.text: Providers ensure compliance with Section 2, have a quality management system, keep documentation and logs, undergo conformity assessment (Art. 43), draw up an EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), affix CE marking (Art. 48), register (Art. 49), take corrective actions (Art. 20) and demonstrate conformity on request.

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
obligations.text: Before deployment, bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III 5(b) (creditworthiness) and 5(c) (life and health insurance) systems perform an assessment of: the deployer's processes using the system; period and frequency of use; categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected; specific risks of harm to them; human oversight measures; measures to be taken if risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms.

obligations.title: Conformity assessment
obligations.text: High-risk systems undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market; for most Annex III systems this is internal control (Annex VI).

obligations.title: Registration
obligations.text: Providers (and public-authority deployers) register Annex III high-risk systems in the EU database before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

obligations.title: Transparency: interaction with natural persons
obligations.text: Providers ensure AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed so those persons are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious from the context.

obligations.title: Post-market monitoring
obligations.text: Providers establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the risk, actively collecting and analysing data on performance throughout the lifetime.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
obligations.text: Before deployment, bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III 5(b) (creditworthiness) and 5(c) (life and health insurance) systems perform an assessment of: the deployer's processes using the system; period and frequency of use; categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected; specific risks of harm to them; human oversight measures; measures to be taken if risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
